To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mtDNA-1038A polymorphism, a genetic risk factor for bipolar disorder (BD), is associated with lower brain glucose utilizations in BD patients and their unaffected siblings.
the mitochondrial DNA 103980A polymorphism, a risk factor for bipolar disorder, affects glucose utilisation in the brain and is associated with insulin resistance in the blood.
the A10398G mitochondrial DNA polymorphism is associated with insulin resistance and cognitive deficits in patients with bipolar disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis for brain GU and its relationship to insulin resistance.
the genetic, physiological and behavioral consequences of mtDNA-103988A in BD.
the functional effect of mtDNA-103998A on the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mtDNA-103998A polymorphism is a risk factor in BD and is associated with abnormal glucose metabolism in the brain and body, which may be the mechanism underlying the pathophysiology of BD.
BD-pairs carry more mtDNA- 10398A and have abnormal glucose metabolism in brain, and the abnormality is associated with the polymorphism.
the mtDNA 10398A is associated with insulin resistance, abnormal prefrontal-GUs and cognitive functions in BD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial energy deficiency in the prefrontal cortex of BD-pairs was compensated by an up-regulation of brain glucose utilization, which may lead to insulin resistance.
the mtDNA-103998A polymorphism may lead to a dysfunctional brain energy metabolism and cognitive functions in BD.
the mitochondrial dysfunction caused by mtDNA-1038A polymorphism leads to impaired prefrontal GU and cognitive functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial DNA 103980 polymorphism may play a role in the pathophysiology of BD.
the brain glucose utilizations and cognitive functions are modulated by mitochondrial genetic variations.
mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to the development of BD by affecting glucose utilization in the brain.
